pool.text: Officially, Samara started with a fortress built at the confluence of the Volga rivers.
A local customs office was established in the city during the early period.
Samara was turned into an uyezd town of Simbirsk Governorate overseen by officials.
Samara became the centre of Samara Governorate with an estimated population of residents.
A mission from the Samara City Duma brought a special banner to Bulgaria.
The regional museum of local history was founded as one of the oldest.
Samara was renamed to Kuybyshev in honor of the Russian Bolshevik Valerian Kuybyshev.
The Communist Party and governmental organisations were evacuated to the city during wartime.
The wartime evacuation decisions affecting the city organisations were reversed during summer.
Kuybyshev became the missile shield centre for the country during the era.
Yuri Gagarin took a rest in Kuybyshev after returning from his space flight.
Grushinsky festival was established as an annual Russian bard song festival.
An unusual ground-attack aircraft monument was placed on display at a major intersection.
The city reverted to its historical name of Samara from Kuybyshev.
A new exposition exhibiting previously classified top secret materials was opened.
Samara hosted the European Union—Russia Summit during the month of May.
Rock over Volga international rock festival was held annually timed to Russia Day.
Samara's nine city districts were granted municipal status during the spring.
Samara was awarded the title City of Labor and Combat Glory by authorities.
Samara became one of the host cities of the FIFA World Cup matches.
